$comment: Committed expected failure counts for the Slice-0 thesis invariants.
These numbers are MEASURED, never predicted. Each check exits 0 iff its finding
count equals the number here — a count that DROPS is red too, which forces the
decrement into the same PR as the fix and makes a silent regression impossible
in either direction. A baseline decremented without an accompanying source
change is visible in review as a one-line diff with no fix beside it.
Every entry is currently NON-ZERO on purpose. An invariant that passes on day
one is measuring nothing. When a `blockedBy` slice lands, that slice decrements
its own baseline; when a baseline reaches 0 the `--expect` gate is removed and
the check switches to zero-tolerance (spec Phase 4).
Measured 2026-07-19 on ci/thesis-invariants against a freshly built compiler

governed.reason: Scorecard §Governed 4/4 — CLEARED 2026-07-19 by GO1 + GO2 in one commit (2→0), the ratchet's first entry to reach zero. Was 2: (1) 'Rate limiting fails closed — ❌ — agent-service.ts:215 — `if (rateLimitSpec !== null && rateLimitPlugin)`. Declare `$rate-limit`, omit the plugin, get silently unlimited' (probe G1). GO1 split the guard so an absent plugin returns 429 RATE_LIMIT_MISSING, mirroring the `$scope`/401 AUTH_MISSING posture. (2) 'Bridge handshake verified — ❌ — BRIDGE_PROTOCOL_VERSION is sent (bridge-client.ts:67) and exported (index.ts:15) — and never checked server-side' (probe G2, one finding covering all three sub-probes: one defect, the absent comparison). GO2 wrote the comparison: `callTool` refuses to delegate to a channel that has not completed a valid `hello` (503 BRIDGE_UNVERIFIED), and an unverified channel may send no frame other than `hello`. The no-bridge headless/CI path (agent-server.ts:279) is untouched and requires no handshake. Both slices landed with bidirectional named tests — a declared control with its plugin absent DENIES, an undeclared control still DISPATCHES — and the probe's self-test was re-based in the same commit from shim-simulated fixes to real-code regressions plus a must-delegate positive control, so it still discriminates rather than going vacuous at zero.
governed.ratchet: CLEARED. GO1 + GO2 landed together and took 2→0. Per spec Phase 4, this entry is now eligible to drop its `--expect` gate and switch to zero-tolerance.

dual-audience.reason: Scorecard §Dual-audience 2/4 — DA-a and DA-b CLEARED 2026-07-20 by DA1 + DA2 in one commit (4→2); DA-c and DA-d remain ❌. (DA-a) CLEARED by DA1: RouteMarkdownResolver, a real exported class in packages/plugin-agent-readiness/src/markdown-resolver.ts, published from the package public entry. It projects route declarations (@route head title/description/body) plus the @aihu/agent component registry into markdown — NOT an HTML re-serialization, which thesis §1 explicitly disqualifies ('an agent surface that is merely the UI re-serialized has failed this property') and which Cloudflare already does better at the edge. (DA-b) CLEARED by DA2: content-negotiation.ts now falls back to user-agent matching when the client expressed no format preference, reusing the SAME AI_BOT_LIST that robots.txt is generated from (a second list would be a check:derived violation). Bidirectional by construction — an explicit Accept: text/html beats any crawler UA, so a browser can never be handed markdown. The DA-b self-test was re-based in the same commit: its should-flag case now simulates a REAL-CODE regression (userAgentFallback: false, a production option) instead of simulating the fix, because a simulated fix goes vacuous the moment the fix is real. Verified after the change: check:dual-audience reports 2 findings, self-test ok (8 cases, both directions), and still FAILS as it must. (DA-c) 'Primary content retrievable without JS — ❌ — packages/router/src/server.ts:41 — renderToString(component) with no options, so the production path emits non-hydratable output' (one finding covering both DA-c assertions: one defect, the missing options object). (DA-d) 'Statically prerendered content retrievable without JS — ❌ — packages/app/src/prerender.ts:283 and :382 — renderToString(...) with no options, so every SSG page ships non-hydratable output' (one finding: one defect, the missing options object in the SSG writer).
dual-audience.expectChangedReason: RATCHET DECREMENT 4→2 by DA1 + DA2, landed together on fix/markdown-negotiation. Two real defects fixed, each with bidirectional named tests; see `reason` for what each fix was. The prior entry (4←3, 2026-07-19) is retained below for the audit trail. PRIOR: FOUNDER SCOPE DECISION (2026-07-19) — not a regression, and not a newly introduced defect. Prerender was ruled IN SCOPE for the dual-audience property, so check:dual-audience gained the DA-d probe and now measures 4 where it measured 3. NOTHING WAS FIXED by this change and nothing broke: packages/app/src/prerender.ts:283/:382 have always called renderToString(...) with no options — the check simply did not look at the SSG path, so a shipping defect went unmeasured. Verified after the change: check:dual-audience reports 4 findings and still FAILS, as it must. DA-d is a SEPARATE finding from DA-c rather than a widening of it, because they are separate defects in separate files with separate fixes — DA3 repairing packages/router/src/server.ts does not repair the SSG writer, and grouping them would let one fix silently decrement a baseline covering two live defects.
dual-audience.ratchet: DA1 (MarkdownResolver) + DA2 (UA negotiation) LANDED TOGETHER and took 4→2, so the planned 4→3→2 intermediate step was never observed. DA3 (after CO5, path keys must agree first) takes 2→1; DA3b (hydratable options in the SSG writer, packages/app/src/prerender.ts) takes 1→0. DA3 and DA3b are tracked separately on purpose: the router fix and the prerender fix are independent edits.
